name: Monthly profit and loss (P&L)
period: Last 2 fiscal years plus year to date
why_buyers_ask: A buyer starts every earnings analysis from the monthly P&L. Send both bases if you keep both.

name: Monthly balance sheet
why_buyers_ask: The balance sheet shows cash, receivables, payables, and debt. A buyer uses it to set the working capital target.

name: General ledger detail
why_buyers_ask: The ledger lists every entry behind the P&L. A buyer reads it to test cash, expenses, and one-time items.

name: Bank statements, all accounts
why_buyers_ask: Bank records are the one source the books cannot change. A buyer ties deposits and balances to your reports.

name: Bank reconciliations
why_buyers_ask: A signed reconciliation shows that someone matched the books to the bank each month. Gaps raise doubt about every number.

name: Sales by customer, monthly
why_buyers_ask: This report shows who pays you and how much. A buyer tests customer concentration and ties sales to the P&L.

name: Expenses by vendor, monthly
why_buyers_ask: This report shows where the money goes. A buyer looks for one-time costs, personal costs, and vendors tied to the owner.

name: Accounts receivable (AR) and accounts payable (AP) aging
why_buyers_ask: Aging shows who owes you and whom you owe. A buyer finds old unpaid invoices and unrecorded bills here.

name: Tax returns
why_buyers_ask: A buyer compares the revenue on your tax return with the revenue in your books. A large gap needs an explanation.

name: Payroll summaries by employee per year
why_buyers_ask: Payroll is often the largest cost. A buyer checks owner pay against what a replacement manager would cost.

name: Form 1096 and Form 1099 filings
why_buyers_ask: Missing 1099 forms show a compliance gap. A buyer also uses them to find contractors who work like employees.

name: Owner list of one-time or non-recurring items
why_buyers_ask: A buyer adds back costs that will not repeat. Your list gives the buyer a place to start, and you control the story.

name: Proposed adjustments with support
why_buyers_ask: A buyer accepts an adjustment only with a document behind it. An adjustment with no support often gets dropped.

name: Related-party transaction schedule
why_buyers_ask: Deals with family or owner entities may not be at market rates. A buyer restates them to market terms.

name: Leases and rent terms
why_buyers_ask: A buyer needs the go-forward rent. If you own the building, rent must reflect what the buyer will pay.

name: Accounting policies and policy changes
why_buyers_ask: A change in policy can move earnings between years. A buyer wants to see what changed and why.

name: Reviews, compilations, or audits
why_buyers_ask: An outside accountant's report gives a buyer more comfort in your numbers. A buyer asks if one exists.

name: Org chart and owner transition plan
why_buyers_ask: A buyer prices the risk that the business depends on you. A clear transition plan lowers that risk.

name: Confidential information memorandum (CIM) and letter of intent (LOI)
why_buyers_ask: A QoE tests the claims in these documents. The numbers in your marketing must match your books.

name: Statement of cash flows
why_buyers_ask: This statement shows where cash came from and where it went. A buyer checks it against the bank.

name: Subscription export from the billing system
period: All subscriptions active in the last 24 months
why_buyers_ask: It lists each customer, plan, billing interval, start date, end date, and amount. A buyer rebuilds recurring revenue from it.

name: Contracts for the 20 largest customers by ARR
why_buyers_ask: A buyer reads contract terms for length, renewal, and exit rights. These terms decide how safe the revenue is.

name: Deferred revenue schedule
why_buyers_ask: Customers who pay in advance create a liability. A buyer ties your schedule to the balance sheet.

name: Monthly MRR or ARR report
why_buyers_ask: Buyers price a SaaS business on recurring revenue. They test your report against billing and the P&L.

name: Capitalized software policy and schedule
why_buyers_ask: Capitalized development costs raise earnings. A buyer checks that you applied the policy the same way each year.

name: Commission plan and payout records
why_buyers_ask: Sales commissions are a real cost of growth. A buyer checks how you treat commissions on annual contracts.

name: Inventory at each period end
period: Same as the monthly balance sheet
why_buyers_ask: Inventory is cash tied up in stock. A buyer tests counts, old stock, and write-downs.

name: Work in progress (WIP) schedule at each period end
period: Same as the monthly balance sheet
why_buyers_ask: Unfinished jobs affect revenue timing. A buyer checks that you book revenue as the work is done.
